nodes.label: GitHub Sponsors funding button
nodes.rationale: github: entry requires GitHub Sponsors to be enabled on the account; ko_fi/custom are noted as instant, no-approval alternatives.

nodes.label: Bug report issue template
nodes.rationale: Asks for norn --version, OS/arch and agent.command so reports carry the fields that actually determine reproducibility.

nodes.label: Feature request issue template
nodes.rationale: Framed problem-first ("what does norn make hard today") rather than solution-first, so ideas arrive with their motivation.

nodes.label: Roadmap contact link (issue chooser)
nodes.rationale: Points filers at open issues + milestones first to cut duplicates; blank issues stay enabled so nothing is blocked by the templates.

nodes.label: Tag-triggered release workflow
nodes.rationale: Fires only on v* tags so releases are an explicit act; fetch-depth 0 is required for GoReleaser to diff tags for the changelog.

nodes.label: HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN cross-repo secret
nodes.rationale: A separate PAT with contents:write on Sandbye/homebrew-norn is needed because the default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot write to another repository.

nodes.label: norn cross-platform build matrix
nodes.rationale: CGO_ENABLED=0 keeps the binary static and portable; darwin+linux x amd64+arm64 covers the target audience; -s -w -X main.version stamps the version read by norn --version.

nodes.label: Homebrew cask distribution
nodes.rationale: Cask, not formula: the modern GoReleaser path for pre-compiled binaries. The post-install hook strips com.apple.quarantine so the unsigned binary is not blocked by Gatekeeper. macOS only, Linux users take the raw release asset.

nodes.label: Changelog commit filters
nodes.rationale: Excludes docs:, test: and chore: Conventional Commit prefixes so the generated release notes only carry user-visible change.

nodes.label: norn (worktree + agent-session TUI)
nodes.rationale: Named for the Norns weaving threads of fate at the world tree: worktrees are the threads, git is the tree. Tagline "many threads, one tree".

nodes.label: One worktree per task
nodes.rationale: Isolated checkout per task removes stashing and branch-juggling when switching between parallel pieces of work.

nodes.label: Single tabbed TUI program
nodes.rationale: One process with Tab / 1-4 switching replaces separate commands, so context stays in one place; ? shows keys, esc backs out, q quits.

nodes.label: Threads tab (worktree dashboard)
nodes.rationale: Live view across repos of branch, PR state and age; enter cd's in, o opens the agent, / filters, m jumps to the main checkout.

nodes.label: New tab (create worktree from hint)
nodes.rationale: Hint becomes a Conventional Branch name; T seeds from a real tracker task, M picks the model.

nodes.label: Clean tab (prune merged/gone worktrees)
nodes.rationale: Auto-selects worktrees whose work is merged or whose remote branch is gone so pruning is one keystroke rather than an audit.

nodes.label: Settings tab (in-place config editing)
nodes.rationale: Edits agent, template, theme and toggles with a global/project layer switch, writing YAML surgically so comments and hand-added keys survive.

nodes.label: shell-init cd integration
nodes.rationale: A child process cannot change its parent shell's directory, so a shell wrapper is eval'd from the binary itself; shipping it inside the binary means it never drifts from the implementation. Optional, norn degrades to not moving the shell.

nodes.label: norn review <pr#>
nodes.rationale: Checks the PR branch out into a worktree so the agent reviews real code it can read, run and comment on, fork PRs included, rather than a text diff.

nodes.label: norn diff viewer
nodes.rationale: For a quick read without spending a worktree: uncommitted changes, branch-vs-base, or any open PR, with split view and syntax highlighting.

nodes.label: --since-review comment overlay
nodes.rationale: Overlays your own review comments, including outdated ones, next to the current code so comment and fix are readable in one scroll.

nodes.label: Local agent review to .norn/review.md
nodes.rationale: Reviewing the agent should not require a PR or a public repo. R writes comments grouped by file, anchored path:line, blocking count at the top, then resumes the agent pointed at it so one pass replaces a dozen round-trips. .norn/ belongs in .gitignore because the review is yours, not part of the change.

nodes.label: Conventional-comment labels in review
nodes.rationale: Each comment gets a conventionalcomments.org label with one key (i/s/n/q/t/p/h/o) plus b for blocking, so intent is explicit and cheap to type.

nodes.label: Configurable coding agent (agent.command)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code is the default but any CLI agent works: with claude the brief is injected via --append-system-prompt and resumed with -c; other agents are launched in the worktree where .worktree.md carries the brief. Thread summaries and AI branch naming are Claude-only and simply do not run otherwise.

nodes.label: .worktree.md brief templates
nodes.rationale: Ships task and review; user files in ~/.config/work/templates/<name>.md.tmpl shadow a built-in so customization never forks the binary.

nodes.label: Tracker task seeding (github | clickup)
nodes.rationale: norn only seeds branch name and hint from a tracker task; the agent's own MCP does the deep work, so norn deliberately is not an MCP client. github reuses existing gh auth so no token is needed.

nodes.label: Theme system (nord, frog)
nodes.rationale: nord is arctic frost + aurora, frog is mossy greens with a dashboard avatar; a palette is a few lines in internal/tui/styles.go, kept cheap on purpose to invite PRs.

nodes.label: Zero-config with layered overrides
nodes.rationale: Works with no config at all; norn init scaffolds a per-project file, global defaults live in ~/.config/work/config.yaml, and --project-config / doctor make the resolved state inspectable.

nodes.label: Graceful degradation of optional tooling
nodes.rationale: Only git is required. gh unlocks PR features and claude launches sessions, but both are optional so a missing tool disables a feature instead of breaking the program.

nodes.label: norn package architecture
nodes.rationale: cmd/work/main.go routes CLI args; internal/{config,git,tui,prompt,review} separate config loading, git operations, Bubble Tea views, template rendering and the review model.

nodes.label: Composable config (global + per-project)
nodes.rationale: Global defaults plus per-repo .work.yaml overrides, so no repo-specific knowledge is hardcoded into the binary.

nodes.label: Remote branch check in clean
nodes.rationale: git fetch --prune then existence check on origin/<branch> yields a gone/active flag per worktree, which is the real signal for whether a worktree is safe to delete.

nodes.label: Age from last commit, not filesystem mtime
nodes.rationale: Commit date is a more meaningful staleness measure than mtime, which any build or editor touch would reset.
nodes.norm_label: age from last commit, not filesystem mtime

nodes.label: Direct create shortcut
nodes.rationale: work "hint" bypasses the TUI entirely and picks the first base branch, optimizing the common fast-path over generality.

nodes.label: ExecProcess terminal handoff to the agent
nodes.rationale: tea.ExecProcess hands terminal control to Claude so the alt screen exits cleanly instead of fighting the agent for the TTY.
nodes.norm_label: execprocess terminal handoff to the agent

nodes.label: Prompt generation via text/template
nodes.rationale: internal/prompt renders .worktree.md from config plus a selected template. Precedence is --template flag, then cfg.template (task), then kind; user overrides live in ~/.config/work/templates.

nodes.label: One review flow, two sinks
nodes.rationale: The diff view's comment machinery is shared: PR mode POSTs to GitHub, local mode writes .norn/review.md and offers to resume the agent. Comments carry a conventional-comment label and blocking flag rendered into the body for both sinks, so there is one keymap to learn.

nodes.label: Repo contribution conventions
nodes.rationale: Conventional Commits title-only by default with a body only when the why is non-obvious; Conventional Branch <type>/<title>; concise PRs with no test-plan section unless asked.

nodes.label: Headless Claude integration
nodes.rationale: Turns norn from a launcher into an orchestrator: drive claude -p non-interactively and render results inline without opening a session. --bare skips hook/skill/MCP/CLAUDE.md discovery for deterministic machine-identical runs, with context passed explicitly.

nodes.label: internal/claude Run + Options design
nodes.rationale: Shells out with cmd.Dir = dir and parses the JSON envelope; driven from the TUI as a tea.Cmd goroutine so the event loop never blocks, with context.WithTimeout because headless can be slow even with --bare.

nodes.label: Dashboard session summarize (MVP use case)
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the first headless use case because it is read-only and low risk while still proving the integration end to end.

nodes.label: Headless cost and permission gates
nodes.rationale: Surface .total_cost_usd per call since headless/SDK calls may bill from a separate credit pool; keep --allowedTools minimal to read + git-read so no prompts appear, and never use --dangerously-skip-permissions.

nodes.label: PR review-since-stamp diff
nodes.rationale: Diffing reviewSHA..HEAD in the existing unified viewer makes the old side the code as reviewed and the added lines the fix, so comment and new code sit in one scroll. Side-by-side was rejected as an expensive two-column rewrite that is not the actual win.

nodes.label: GitHub outdated-comment limitation
nodes.rationale: GitHub drops a reviewer's comment from the Files-changed diff once the author edits that line, so comment and new code cannot be seen together even across all commits. Confirmed limitation, community thread #23138.

nodes.label: Review-stamp SHA resolution via gh api
nodes.rationale: Latest own review by submitted_at gives .commit_id as BASE; two-dot equals three-dot because HEAD descends from it. Fallbacks: no own review falls back to base...HEAD with a note, null original_line falls back to original_position, and comments outside the diff surface in a tail so nothing is hidden.
nodes.norm_label: review-stamp sha resolution via gh api

nodes.label: Local code review (shipped)
nodes.rationale: Comment any local diff with conventional-comment labels; R writes .norn/review.md and resumes the agent against it, so no PR and no public repo are required.

nodes.label: Rebrand work to norn
nodes.rationale: Module, GitHub repo, Nord theme, "many threads, one tree" identity, MIT license and README all moved together.

nodes.label: Public launch v0.1.0
nodes.rationale: VHS demo GIF plus a leaner README, Homebrew cask and tag-triggered release workflow, public repo and tap.

nodes.label: Multi-agent teams deliberately out of scope
nodes.rationale: Agent teams, peer-to-peer agent messaging and shared task lists with auto-dependency resolution target teams of agents coordinating on one feature, which is over-engineering for a solo one-agent-per-worktree setup. Revisit only at 5+ parallel agents on a single feature.
nodes.norm_label: multi-agent teams deliberately out of scope

nodes.label: Backlog as GitHub Issues and Milestones
nodes.rationale: Live backlog moved out of the markdown file into Issues grouped by area/* labels, with a milestone per release, so the roadmap file keeps only shipped items and design write-ups.
nodes.norm_label: backlog as github issues and milestones
